opex.text: Operating expenses were $24.0 million and $71.3 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $20.7 million and $63.0 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. Such amounts were inclusive of salaries and employee benefits of $10.8 million and $33.0 million during the current quarter and nine-month period, compared to $10.1 million and $30.3 million for the prior year periods, with the increase reflecting higher costs associated with a greater head count at our operating subsidiary, Medallion Bank, and higher equity compensation costs in the current nine month period. Additionally, other expenses were higher, particularly loan servicing expense and regulatory costs, reflecting our growing loan portfolio. We expect our operating expenses to further increase as we continue to build capacity as part of our growth strategy.

costs.text: Operating expenses were $24.0 million and $71.3 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $20.7 million and $63.0 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. Such amounts were inclusive of salaries and employee benefits of $10.8 million and $33.0 million during the current quarter and nine-month period, compared to $10.1 million and $30.3 million for the prior year periods, with the increase reflecting higher costs associated with a greater head count at our operating subsidiary, Medallion Bank, and higher equity compensation costs in the current nine month period. Additionally, other expenses were higher, particularly loan servicing expense and regulatory costs, reflecting our growing loan portfolio. We expect our operating expenses to further increase as we continue to build capacity as part of our growth strategy.

prov.text: The provision for credit losses was $30.8 million and $75.5 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $18.6 million and $62.1 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The provision for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 included net charge-offs of $19.6 million and $56.4 million, compared to $14.4 million and $48.4 million in the prior year periods, with recreation loans accounting for $16.3 million and $47.3 million compared to $12.9 million and $41.1 million in the prior year. Credit provisions were $1.0 million and $2.2 million for commercial loans for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.4 million and $7.4 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The provision for credit losses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 reflected the impact of growth of our consumer loan portfolio, particularly the recreation loan portfolio, which grew 5% during the quarter and 15% during the nine month period, and which required an allowance for credit losses of approximately $5.6 million and $14.2 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Additionally, fluctuations in portfolio aging and other economic factors caused us to adjust our allowance coverage ratios.

Such amounts were inclusive of salaries and employee benefits of $10.8 million and $33.0 million during the current quarter and nine-month period, compared to $10.1 million and $30.3 million for the prior year periods, with the increase reflecting higher costs associated with a greater head count at our operating subsidiary, Medallion Bank, and higher equity compensation costs in the current nine month period. Additionally, other expenses were higher, particularly loan servicing expense and regulatory costs, reflecting our growing loan portfolio. nonop.text: Our interest expense is driven by the interest rates payable on our bank certificates of deposit, privately placed notes, fixed-rate, long-term debentures issued to the SBA, trust preferred securities, and has historically included credit facilities with banks and other short-term notes payable. The Bank issues brokered time certificates of deposit, non-brokered time deposits and high yield savings accounts, which are, on average, our lowest borrowing costs. The Bank is able to bid on these deposits at a variety of maturity options, which allows for more flexible interest rate management strategies.

net.text: Net income attributable to Medallion Financial Corp. was $2.4 million and $14.8 million, or $0.10 and $0.61 per diluted share, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7.8 million and $30.8 million, or $0.32 and $1.28 per diluted share, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.text: Our loan-related earnings depend primarily on our level of net interest income. Net interest income is the difference between the total yield on our loan portfolio and the average cost of borrowed funds. We fund our operations through a wide variety of interest-bearing sources, including bank certificates of deposit issued to consumers, privately placed notes, debentures issued to and guaranteed by the SBA, trust preferred securities, and preferred stock of the Bank. Net interest income fluctuates with changes in the yield on our loan portfolios and changes in the cost of borrowed funds, as well as changes in the amount of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities held by us.

intro.text: Medallion Financial Corp. (NASDAQ: MFIN) and its subsidiaries originate and service a portfolio of consumer loans and mezzanine loans in various industries. Key industries served include recreation (towable RVs and marine) and home improvement (swimming pools, replacement roofs, and windows). Medallion Financial Corp. is headquartered in New York City, NY, and its largest subsidiary, Medallion Bank, is headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah. For more information, please visit www.medallion.com .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
